newsitem.title: UK: Mideast/Japan crude tankers sparky again.
newsitem.headline: Mideast/Japan crude tankers sparky again.

text.p: Chartering rates for 250,000 tonne Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) were steamy again on Wednesday and brokers said numbers could rise yet more.
Dealers said the W87 paid for the 255,000 tonne Tarim to load in late August was on the money.

"It is still strong, and rising," one broker said. "There are not a lot of ships available. Anyone left with a cargo to move is in for a messy shock - I would say W85 would be a good price to pay at the moment."

Analysts attributed the high prices - which compare to roughly W45-50 in April - are because of an end to refinery turnarounds in Asia combined with the beginning of inventory building ahead of the northern hemisphere's winter.

North Sea-transatlantic routes were very quiet, however, for million-barrel and two-million barrel tankers. But some guessed that stronger crude oil prices in the U.S., buoyed by oil inventory data released overnight showing a 10 million barrel weekly crude stocks drawdown, could open up the route again.
Shorter-haul Caribs/upcoast U.S. routes were firm again and dealers said 70,000 tonne tankers plying routes to the U.S. Gulf were easily commanding W137.50.
West African million-barrel cargoes were little changed with a few ships seen fixed at around W77.5-W80, and the 260,000 tonners were pegged at around W67.50.
